title: Class 2 (lunch): Decorate it, give it eyes

series.title: Physical AI Lab: Build a Robot Desk Assistant (5 classes)

summary: A lunchtime build session. Decorate your robot with the supplies on the table, and if you want, add the eyes upgrade: two moving eyes that glance around while it talks and that it can cross or point when you ask.
detail: Bring your robot from Class 1. Most of the hour is decorating: we bring the supplies. Want more? Pick up an eyeball kit: two eyeballs, two small servos and four wires. They go in behind the face, plug into the same breadboard, and the robot program on your Pico already knows how to drive them. Tick My robot has moving eyes on this page, and your robot gets two new function calls: cross its eyes, and look left or right. While it talks, its eyes glance around on their own.
outcome: A decorated robot with its own look and, if you took the upgrade, eyes that move while it talks and on request.
artifact: A decorated talking robot, optionally with moving eyes driven by function calls.
prereqs: Your robot from Class 1, with its Pico and breadboard.
Your laptop with Google Chrome, and your Deepgram API key.
Everything else is on the table: decorating supplies, and eyeball kits for the eyes upgrade.

slides.title: Class 2: Decorate it, give it eyes
bullets: Lunch, glue and googly eyes.
Everyone decorates. Want moving eyes? Grab an eyeball kit.
Eat first, glue second: keep food away from the electronics.
slides.note: A relaxed lunch class. Show off a decorated robot with moving eyes at the start so people know what's possible.

slides.title: What each robot needs today
bullets: ☐ Your robot from Class 1, with its Pico and breadboard
☐ Decorating supplies, on the table
Eyes upgrade (optional): ☐ 2 × eyeballs ☐ 2 × MG90S servos with horns ☐ 2 × male-to-female jumper wires (signal) ☐ 4 × male-to-male jumper wires (power)
☐ Glue gun (one per table, with a helper nearby)
Bring: your laptop and your Deepgram key
slides.note: Dana brings the eyeballs. Pre-bag the eye kits so people grab one and go. Every Pico already runs the program with eyes support (it's loaded at Class 1 check-in), so nobody reloads anything. If someone joined late with a blank Pico, load it at the helper table like Class 1.

slides.title: Give it a look
bullets: Hair, ears, a hat, a cape: make it look like its personality.
Keep the mouth flap free to move, and don't glue over the servo.
Leave the back open so you can reach the wires.
slides.note: Walk the room with a robot that talks while people work. Remind anyone doing eyes to cut the eye holes before they decorate the face.

slides.title: Mount the eyes
bullets: Cut two holes in the face, above the mouth, just big enough for the eyeballs.
Glue each eyeball to the top of a servo horn, then push the horn onto its servo.
From inside, glue each servo behind its hole so the eyeball sits in the hole and can turn left and right.
Turn each eyeball gently by hand: it should swing freely.
slides.note: Check this against the eyeballs Dana brings and adjust the hole size. Done when: both eyes turn freely by hand without catching the face.

slides.title: Wire the eyes
bullets: Left eye's orange wire to GP13 (pin 17), right eye's to GP12 (pin 16), with male-to-female jumpers.
Both reds to the breadboard's + row, both browns to the − row, like the mouth.
Nothing new goes on the Pico's power pins.
Plug the Pico back into your laptop.
slides.note: Left and right mean the robot's left and right, as if you were the robot. Pins 16 and 17 are on the left side, just above GP14 (pin 19) and GP15 (pin 20). Helpers check every board before it's plugged in.

slides.title: Switch them on
bullets: Connect the robot, then open Eyes under Plug in your robot.
Tick My robot has moving eyes.
Press Cross eyes, Look left and Look right to test.
Start talking and ask it to cross its eyes. Watch the Tool line: that's a function call moving real hardware.
slides.note: If they cross outward, swap the two eye wires (GP12 and GP13). The eyes switch off when the robot is quiet, so they don't buzz. If nothing moves at all, the Pico has the old program: load the current one at the helper table.

slides.title: Meet the neighbours
bullets: Turn to the next table and introduce your robot.
Let it introduce itself too.
Film a clip with Film a clip and share it with #RobotLunchLab.

slides.title: Class 3: more personalities, more skills
bullets: Give your robot more personalities and switch between them by voice.
Pick its skills: Muni trips, timers, notes, look-ups and more.
Bring your robot and your Deepgram key.

flow.title: Test your robot
flow.note: Connect your robot, then tick My robot has moving eyes under Eyes if you added them.

flow.title: Show and tell, and next class

troubleshooting: The eyes don't move at all: check the orange wires are on GP13 (pin 17) and GP12 (pin 16), and the reds and browns are on the + and − rows. Still nothing? The Pico has an old program: load the current one at the helper table.
The eyes cross outward: swap the left and right eye wires.
Left and right are backwards: swap the two eye wires.
An eye catches on the face: make the hole a little bigger, or move the servo back.
The Pico resets when the eyes move: the eye servos are getting power from the Pico. All reds go to the + row, never to the Pico.
Connect robot does nothing at all: you're not in Chrome. Open the page in Chrome (or Chromium on a Raspberry Pi).
Another program is using the port: quit Thonny and close other tabs with this page, unplug the Pico, plug it back in, and connect again.

The page says the robot reset while talking: a servo is pulling power from the Pico. Check every red wire goes to the + row, the power lead is in a charger or power bank, nothing is on pin 40, and the ground jumper to pin 23 is in.
It cuts you off: raise Patience. It's slow to answer: lower it.
It talks to itself, or stops mid-sentence for no reason: it's hearing its own voice. Switch off Let me interrupt it (barge-in), or move the laptop away from the robot's speaker.
Deepgram stopped the session: check the key was pasted whole, and that the account has credit.
